# `rules/tei/output/` — RDF graphs generated by the pipeline

This folder holds the RDF (Turtle) graphs produced from the reference corpus
`data/zoo/` (89 files: the original text and its English translation for each
work). It is the last stage of the pipeline; what it contains is loaded into
the Corese SPARQL server that feeds the web application.

## Where these files come from

```
data/zoo/zooN/Xy.xml            TEI files (the only corpus the pipeline reads)
   │  xml_to_csv.py              named-entity recognition, alignment with the human
   ▼                             translation, one set of CSV files per XML file
data/pipeline_scripts/output/   zooN_Xy_{metadata,paragraph,link,annotations}.csv
   │  morph_mongo.py
   ▼
MongoDB, database "Ner"         collections Metadata, Paragraph, Link, Annotation
   │  graph-generation.py        XR2RML mappings (rules/tei/*.ttl) run by the
   ▼                             morph-xr2rml jar (rules/)
rules/tei/output/               one graph per work + all.ttl.gz   <- this folder
```


## Content of this folder

| Path | What it is |
|------|------------|
| `zooN_Xy/zooN_Xy.ttl` (89 folders) | Graph of one file, named after `data/zoo/zooN/Xy.xml` (e.g. `zoo55_1e` is Varro's English translation). It merges five partial graphs: paragraphs, metadata, links (the book/chapter/section tree), concept labels and annotations. |
| `all.ttl.gz` | All 89 graphs merged into one file, gzip-compressed (34 MB). Uncompressed it is 265 MB, above GitHub's 100 MB limit, which is why only the compressed file is versioned. |
| `th310.ttl` | The Zoomathia thesaurus (OpenTheso `th310`). The annotations point to its concepts; their labels and hierarchy (`skos:prefLabel`, `skos:member`, `skos:broader`) exist only here. |
| `vocab.ttl` | Static file of DBpedia/Wikidata concept labels (older run). The per-work graphs also carry the labels of the concepts they use. |
| `zoomathia.ttl` | The Zoomathia ontology (`zoo:` classes and properties). |


 
## Regenerating

From `data/pipeline_scripts/` (paths are relative to it), for one file:

```bash
echo "./zoo/zoo55/1e.xml" > targets.txt
python3 xml_to_csv.py targets.txt        # XML -> CSV
echo "zoo55_1e" > prefixes.txt
python3 morph_mongo.py prefixes.txt      # CSV -> MongoDB
cd ../../rules/tei
python3 graph-generation.py ../../data/pipeline_scripts/prefixes.txt
```

**`graph-generation.py` skips every work whose folder already exists here**, so after changing the data in MongoDB (for example after `apply_annotation_filters.py` or `reconcile_annotations.py`) the folders must be moved away first, otherwise `all.ttl` is rebuilt from stale graphs. To force a re-run, first delete the file's CSVs in
`data/pipeline_scripts/output/`, its marker in `data/mongo_loaded/*.done`, its
documents in the four MongoDB collections, and its folder here; otherwise the
steps skip it as already up to date. `graph-generation.py` only regenerates
the listed works but always rebuilds `all.ttl` from every graph in this folder.

Compress the result before committing:

```bash
gzip -9 -n -c all.ttl > all.ttl.gz
```

Every new commit of `all.ttl.gz` adds about 34 MB to the repository history
(compressed files do not diff). If the file is regenerated often, Git LFS is
worth considering.

## Loading into Corese

The Corese container mounts `~/corese_data/` and its profile
(`corese-profile.ttl`) loads `mini.ttl`, `th310.ttl` and `vocab.ttl` from it.
`all.ttl` alone is not enough: without the thesaurus, `skos:member` is absent
and every competency question returns zero rows. The ontology
(`zoomathia.ttl`) is appended too. The annotations are typed
`zoo:AutomaticAnnotation`, and Corese runs with RDFS entailment off, so a
pattern like `?x a oa:Annotation` never matches them (competency question 12
used to ask for it and returned zero rows; it now relies on `oa:hasBody`
alone). Build `mini.ttl` like this:

```bash
gzip -dc all.ttl.gz > all.ttl
cat all.ttl th310.ttl vocab.ttl zoomathia.ttl > ~/corese_data/mini.ttl   # keep a backup of the old one
docker restart corese-zoomathia-web
```

Do not query the SPARQL endpoint while Corese is loading: the logs show
`Read lock while parsing` errors after requests sent during startup, and the
files that follow in the profile may then not be loaded. Wait for loading to
finish, then check that a thesaurus query returns results.

## Pitfalls seen in this run

- **No parentheses in the author or the title of a file.** They end up in the
  work's URI and break the graph generation: the graph came out with no
  paragraphs (Semonides, Hippocrates spurious, Paradoxographus). The author
  name used for the URI is the canonical one from
  `data/repertoire_zoo/auteurs_rows.csv`, not the one written in the XML.
- **Annotations depend on external services** (DBpedia Spotlight, Entity-Fishing,
  Google Translate). Reruns can differ slightly, and an unreachable service
  makes `xml_to_csv.py` retry for a long time.

## Annotation quality filters

Before annotations are loaded into MongoDB (`morph_mongo.py`), `data/pipeline_scripts/annotation_filters.py`
drops mentions that are only a number or a roman numeral, DBpedia pages unrelated to the
annotated word (the page title must match the word, or be a known redirect alias), thesaurus
concepts listed in `annotation_exclusions.json` (polysemous words such as "saw" or "lead"), and
Wikidata entities whose description is a film, band, brand, modern town, etc. The two reference
caches (`dbpedia_aliases.json`, `wikidata_descriptions.json`) are filled by
`refresh_annotation_caches.py`. `reconcile_annotations.py` applies the current filters to an
already loaded MongoDB. Tests: `python3 -m unittest test_annotation_filters`.
